candidate.question: Should the fatigue life prediction use the Basquin equation or the Coffin-Manson relationship for this low-cycle fatigue analysis of a steel pressure vessel nozzle?
candidate.reason: The expected strain amplitude of 0.4% places this analysis in the transition region between high-cycle and low-cycle fatigue regimes. The choice of prediction model affects the estimated fatigue life by up to an order of magnitude.

alternatives.label: Basquin equation (stress-life)
alternatives.description: Use the stress-life approach with the Basquin equation relating stress amplitude to cycles to failure.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Well-established for high-cycle fatigue. May overestimate fatigue life in the low-cycle regime where plastic strain dominates.

alternatives.label: Coffin-Manson relationship (strain-life)
alternatives.description: Use the strain-life approach with the Coffin-Manson relationship relating total strain amplitude to reversals to failure.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Appropriate for low-cycle fatigue where plastic strain is significant. Requires cyclic stress-strain curve data which may not be available for the specific heat treatment condition.

candidate.uncertainty: Cyclic material properties for SA-516 Grade 70 steel at the operating temperature of 350C are interpolated from limited published data.
